verdict.rationale: LaunchDarkly's docs show members can be assigned preset roles or custom roles that override their base role. They also show API tokens can be scoped to restrict which operations they can perform, such as read-only integrations. Together these deliver role-based control over who changes flags and least-privilege tokens. Missing for 10: explicit evidence of per-flag or per-environment resource scoping in role policies (the 'which flags' granularity is only implied), detail on the permission/policy language, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can restrict who can change which flags with roles, permissions, and scoped API tokens

citations.quote: If a member is directly assigned a role, such as a preset role or a role that you create, that role is used instead of the member's base role
You assign roles directly to members when you invite them to LaunchDarkly.
You can scope your API tokens to restrict the set of operations they can perform. For example, you can build an integration that only has read access
